cefrAlignment: Matches C1 vocabulary range ('good command of a broad lexical repertoire including idiomatic expressions and colloquialisms; can select appropriate formulations') with attention to register and collocation; all idioms taught or recommended are current and natural (raining cats and dogs and the piece of cakes/blue sky items appear only as examples of what to avoid).
examFidelity: The IELTS Part 2 task (1 min prep, up to 2 min, four-bullet cue card) is accurate and the model (254 words) now fits 2 minutes at about 130 wpm; Lexical Resource guidance matches the public band 7 descriptor.
fixes: MCQ 'Which sentence uses the idiom correctly?' had two defensible answers, because option D uses 'hit it off' correctly but announces it. Changed it to 'correctly and naturally' and updated the explanation
Gap 'came round to' now also accepts the US variant 'came around to'
Changed the illogical 'The real damage is underground' (river pollution) to 'below the surface', which also fits the iceberg image
Replaced the filler cliché 'at the end of the day' with 'for the time being' as an example fixed phrase, because the lesson tells learners to avoid clichés
Trimmed the Part 2 model from 264 to 254 words (it ran to about 122 s at 130 wpm)
Exam tips: removed the unverified claim that a misused memorised phrase is 'more damaging' and softened 'the best place for idiomatic language'
openConcerns: Model audio is TTS. It will not show how idioms are delivered naturally (stress, chunking)
learnerOutcome: A learner can replace general words with precise collocations, use a few current idioms in their fixed form and the right register, and fit them naturally into a two-minute Part 2 story.
